cands.name: Alicia Escott Lumpkin

money.note: Covers January 2023 on, primary and general. Party-committee lines are often in-kind staff and mail.
money.source: Alabama Fair Campaign Practices Act system, downloaded Nov 5, 2026

cands.bio: Democrat elected to the Alabama House, District 60. Describes herself as a lifelong Birmingham resident with more than 17 years of service with the City of Birmingham. Holds a marketing and logistics degree from the University of Tennessee and a law degree from Birmingham School of Law.

endorsements.text: Tabitha's List: Candidates You Can Trust (voter guide recommendation, Sway voting group by Tabitha Isner), per Ballotpedia.
Birmingham mayor Randall Woodfin backed her bid for the state House, per Wikipedia.

cands.gaps: We could not find where she was born or raised, or when she settled in Birmingham beyond her own description as a lifelong resident. Her exact job titles and duties in 17 years with the City of Birmingham are not documented in the sources we had. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey, and her campaign site lists priorities (economic opportunity, health care, safe communities, veterans) without specific positions or bills. We found no stated positions or actions on data centers, homestead taxes, land ownership, growth, immigration, guns, abortion, policing or school choice, and no documented controversies or foreign ties.

qual.background: More than 17 years working for the City of Birmingham on government efficiency and new initiatives (self-described); holds a Juris Doctor from Birmingham School of Law. No prior elected office found.
qual.why: A long career in local government plus a law degree puts her in the middle band; no prior legislative service was found, and her specific city job title and duties could not be verified.
